chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Musa ibn 'Umar, and Ayyub ibn Nuh, from 'Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abi al-Yasa', who said:

A man asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, saying: 'When I go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), do I make it my qiblah when I pray?' He replied, 'Move aside a little to the side.'
ai.seo_question: Should I face the grave of Imam Husain when praying during Ziyarah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* clarifies the fiqh of facing the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as a qiblah during prayer, a practice rooted in the reverence for the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam’s instruction to 'move aside' signifies that while facing the grave is a recommended act of honor (istiqbal), it is not obligatory (wajib), allowing for flexibility in crowded shrines without obstructing others. This reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that such facing is a sign of respect rather than a strict ritual requirement like facing the Kaaba.
